title: Hunyuan-A13B Technical Report
data_curation: Pretraining reuses the Hunyuan-TurboS pipeline (dedup, low-quality filtering, denoising, topic labeling, model-based extraction, semantic dedup) on a 20T-token corpus, with improved STEM acquisition yielding 250B high-quality STEM tokens plus a knowledge-labeling system and multi-dimensional difficulty grading. Reasoning SFT data: math from textbooks/tests/competitions verified iteratively by generative reward models and automated checkers; code from GitHub via an OSS-Instruct-style pipeline validated by critic models and sandbox execution; ZebraLogic-style synthesized logic puzzles checked by CoT evaluators plus humans; science problems verified by an LLM verifier and rejection sampling. Reasoning RL uses 150K prompts where the SFT model is unstable (math:code:logic:science = 2:2:1:1, 10% overlapping SFT), excluding multiple-choice, true/false and proof problems. Agent SFT data comes from a five-role engine (user, planner, tool, agent, checker), sandbox/MCP/synthetic tools, 30+ system-instruction types and 20,000 format combinations.
curriculum: Pretraining: 20T-token foundation stage (LR warmup to 3e-4, cosine decay to 3e-5 over 13.5T tokens, 4K context), a fast-annealing stage of 300B tokens (3e-5 to 8e-6, 8K context), then long-context extension to 32K and 256K with NTK-aware RoPE (alpha 50 and 1000). Post-training has four sequential steps: reasoning-oriented SFT, then reasoning-oriented RL, then all-scenarios SFT (reasoning data samples mixed with general-domain data), then all-scenarios RL. Reasoning RL itself runs in two context phases, 24K and then 32K.
method: Fine-grained MoE with 80B total / 13B active parameters: 32 layers, 1 always-on shared expert plus 64 non-shared experts with 8 activated, SwiGLU, GQA (32 heads, 8 KV heads), 128K vocabulary. Reasoning RL uses GRPO without the KL term, on-policy updates, large batches, more rollouts, and sampling temperature 0.6-0.8. Rewards come from a lightweight LLM outcome verifier (binary, tolerant of formatting/units/synonyms) and a sandbox for 36 languages that runs 1000+ concurrent executions. All-scenarios RL combines a generative reward model that compares outputs against a reference answer, can read CoT and can call tools, with domain-specific reward services: 16 sub-topics and 30+ scoring services. Examples are paired GRMs for creative writing, hallucination RMs for long context and knowledge QA, and format+correctness rule rewards for agents. Dual-mode CoT trains fast mode (an empty <think> block, '/no think') and slow mode ('/think', the default) in one model.
eval_metrics: Base model: MMLU, MMLU-Pro, MMLU-Redux, BBH, SuperGPQA, EvalPlus, MultiPL-E, MBPP, CRUXEval, MATH, CMATH, GSM8K, GPQA (base scores include MMLU 88.17, MATH 72.35, GSM8K 91.83). Post-trained model: AIME24/25, MATH, GPQA-Diamond, OlympiadBench, LiveCodeBench, FullstackBench, ArtifactsBench (new), BBH, DROP (F1), ZebraLogic, IFEval, SysBench, internal LengthCtrl/InsCtrl/ComplexNLU/Word-Task, and BFCL v3, tau-Bench, ComplexFuncBench, C3-Bench. Slow-thinking results: AIME24 87.3, AIME25 76.8, GPQA-D 71.2, LiveCodeBench 63.9, ZebraLogic 84.7, BFCL v3 78.3, tau-Bench 54.7, C3-Bench 63.5. Long-context results: PenguinScrolls 87.7, LongBench-v2 55.0, FRAMES 81.1, RULER-QA average 76.7 (73.9 at 64K-128K). Throughput at batch 32 is 1981.99 tokens/s.
key_results: With 13B active parameters, Hunyuan-A13B in slow-thinking mode scores 87.3 on AIME2024, ahead of Qwen3-A22B (85.7), DeepSeek-R1 (79.8) and o1 (74.3). It leads all compared models on BFCL v3 (78.3), ComplexFuncBench (61.2) and C3-Bench (63.5), and its base model beats Hunyuan-Large on 12 of 14 benchmarks with 1/4 of the active parameters.
evolution_note: Builds on Hunyuan-Large and Hunyuan-TurboS: it reuses their data pipeline, tokenizer and NTK-aware long-context recipe. Its RL borrows the KL-free GRPO of DAPO and the context-length staging of DeepScaleR. The fast/slow dual-mode CoT with /think and /no think tags follows the hybrid-thinking design of Qwen3. The report is dated 2025-06-27 internally even though its arXiv ID is 2609, so it documents a mid-2025 efficient open MoE that pairs reasoning-first RL with broad generative-reward-model RL.
